newsitem.title: USA: Vallejo, Calif. to assume $52 mln of park debt.
newsitem.headline: Vallejo, Calif. to assume $52 mln of park debt.

text.p: The city of Vallejo, Calif. said on Friday it would assume ownership of the Marine World Africa USA theme park and would take steps to ensure $52 million of its long-term bond obligations are paid in full.
Vallejo City Manager Kenneth Campo said the city would take over on November 1. Campo said the city would take over the park due to its declining attendance and revenues.
"It's time to take a whole new approach," Campo said.

Due to the drop in revenues, Marine World Africa USA is short the funds to fully repay its short-term noteholders, Campo said. The park is short $2 million owed to noteholders on November 1. Campo said noteholders would be paid in full because city funds would be used to offset the shortfall.
The park also has about $52 million of long-term debt, which was issued in 1985 and backed by Vallejo. The city will assume those obligations, Campo said.
The city will assume ownership of the park but will continue with the existing management company, at least for the time being, Campo said.
